source.title: Data Density Scaling Laws for Image Self-Distillation
source.authors: Alvard Barseghyan; Ani Vanyan; H. Tamazyan; Hrant Khachatrian

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports image self-distillation scaling experiments that refine and partly challenge the transfer of existing scaling-law assumptions: downstream results depend on dataset, unique support, repetition, and the fitted law.
record.gate_note: The paper fits laws to downstream accuracy, not held-out pretraining cross-entropy, and studies image self-distillation rather than language models. It reports seven-dataset scaling-law MAEs and separate fixed-budget comparisons. Cited language-model scaling results are not extracted as findings. Numerous curves and per-task or per-seed details are not separate rows where the paper does not give an explicit numeric outcome in the text or tables.
record.test_reason: The study fits power-law-style laws (compute-only Chinchilla-style, data-constrained, prescriptive) to downstream kNN accuracy of iBOT image self-distillation. It fits on runs with C ≤ 50M and checks extrapolation to C > 50M on seven datasets. It also shows that at fixed compute, smaller repeated subsets can beat the full pool. It argues explicitly that data-constrained repeated-data laws do not transfer. The target is frozen-representation accuracy, not pretraining loss. C counts image presentations for a fixed ViT-B recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that image self-distillation scaling depends jointly on compute, unique support and repetition, in a dataset-dependent way. Smaller repeated subsets can beat full data, e.g. on Maxar. The density-interaction law improves held-out prediction on some datasets but not consistently. Note that the Conclusion section claims it gives a better description in the tested range, which overstates Table 1: it is worse on nuPlan, ImageNet and YFCC15M.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses iBOT/DINOv2 image self-distillation and downstream frozen-representation accuracy rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy. It adapts several power-law-style forms and fits on low-compute runs to predict higher-compute transfer performance.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by dataset, compute budget, evaluation protocol (kNN versus logistic regression), model size, self-distillation method, subset-selection method, and augmentation. Known training-loss-spike runs are excluded from the scaling observations.
record.problems: The target is downstream accuracy rather than pretraining loss. The study fixes model/training recipe for its main density sweep and tests only image self-distillation; the authors note that comparisons do not fully separate repetition, redundancy, image quality, and semantic coverage. Statistical reporting includes 124 of 187 matched pairwise comparisons significant at p < 0.05, but the scaling-law MAE table gives no confidence intervals. Some conclusions rely on plotted curves.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row cap. Figure-only density curves and detailed per-task/per-seed outcomes were not separately extracted where the text does not state a distinct numeric result.

untested.parts: All: no loss extrapolation for language models.
All: no parameter/token compute-optimal split; model size fixed in the scaling sweep.
All: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Pretraining loss in image SSL, model-size scaling, video-model training, fine-tuning/transfer laws.
Language-model downstream tasks; prediction from pretraining loss.
Language-model exponents, compute-optimal split, parameter counting, schedule effects.

missing.what: ImageNet is support-limited at C=100M: full 0.6956 vs half-U 0.6545 kNN, consistent with unique data helping.
Waymo is repetition-tolerant: 4–16x smaller U changes accuracy only weakly. Loss-spike runs (0.7714 to 0.5804) were excluded.
Logistic-regression scaling-law MAE. Compute-only extrapolation: Maxar 0.0089, Waymo 0.0018, ImageNet 0.0249. Density law: 0.0070, 0.0037, 0.0112. Law ranking changes with evaluation protocol.
Maxar high-compute degradation is much less visible under logistic regression than kNN, so the bend depends on the evaluation protocol.
Ablation variants of the density law (unique-only, repeat-only, separate, raw-U, raw-R) give different extrapolation errors.

record.verdict_notes: All evidence is downstream frozen-representation accuracy in image SSL, not pretraining loss. Compute is image presentations at a fixed ViT-B recipe, so parameter scaling is not swept. V6 and V7 are read in this image setting; if they are meant for language models only, re-mark them untested. The reader's blanket 'partial' states were replaced with MAE-based states. Density-interaction rows are the study's own proposed law and are linked only to V7. Rows r39–r40 are an augmentation ablation.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out language-model pretraining loss, nor power-law loss sweep over parameters, tokens, or compute.
The extrapolation target is downstream accuracy, not held-out pretraining loss of larger language-model runs.
No language-model parameter/token allocation sweep or compute-optimal split.
No controlled depth, width, or architecture-shape comparison at fixed parameter count.

Tests image self-distillation on image datasets and frozen-representation transfer, including repeated exposure. Does not test video-model training, other modalities, fine-tuning, or whether held-out pretraining loss follows the same form.
Tests prediction of downstream accuracy from smaller-compute runs; does not test language-model downstream tasks or prediction from pretraining loss.

Tests dataset- and law-dependent fitting and extrapolation for downstream accuracy in image self-distillation. Does not directly test language-model loss exponents or the language-model compute-optimal parameter/token split.

rows.subject: iBOT ViT-B/16 on Maxar
rows.operation_detail: Compare random-subset pretraining with full-pool pretraining at matched image-presentation budget.

conditions.value: random subset containing 1.5% of Full pool

rows.measure: average downstream kNN performance difference
rows.baseline: Full 50M-image pool at the same budget
rows.note: Explicit example of repeated training on a smaller pool outperforming the full pool under matched compute.
rows.check: A 1.5% subset beats the full pool by 3.11 pp at 200M, so more unique data is worse at fixed compute. V6 and V7 links dropped.

source_check.correct: Random 1.5% Maxar subset improves average downstream kNN performance by 3.11 percentage points over the full 50M-image pool at 200M presentations. This matched-compute comparison does not determine whether a power-law form holds; V5 state: cannot_determine.
source_check.locator_found: Introduction, paragraph beginning with the 1.5% Maxar example.
source_check.problem: V5 concerns power-law form, not an unconditional benefit from more unique images at fixed compute.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: Maxar image self-distillation at fixed compute (ViT-S/B/L, iBOT and DINOv2, four subset methods)
